items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: he picked up me and my brother, Gus, and Roy Eldridge from Detroit... So the Speed Webb band had Jonesey on one trumpet, Roy Eldridge on the other... and Roy and Vic and I

ctx.x: And the hit song from On With the Show, was the song, 'Am I Blue,' and so Speed Webb, since he had prominent spot as a bandleader in the movie, he wanted to tour and do personal appearances, so he picked up me and my brother, Gus, and Roy Eldridge from Detroit and took us down to his home town in Muncie, Indiana, and he got Vic Zach Dickenson away from the White band, or the West Helmet band, another road band; and we spent oh, a couple of weeks down there in Muncie rehearsing, and he got some other musicians
from Indiana, Reunald Jones from the Atlanta band; Reunald Jones finally wound up, some years ago, he was lead trumpet fo Basie, back about 20 years ago.

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: It was Cozy Cole, John Kirby, Teddy Wilson, Chu Berry and myself.

ctx.x: You hadn't run into Art Tatum yet, though.
No, I didn't run into Art Tatum until I was with McKinney's Cotton Pickers. I ran into him in 1933 or '34. Then we did a lot of playing together.

But I had been to New York, see. I was in New York, and I worked with Cecil Scott first at the Les Maison(?), and from the Les Maison(?)... Did I go to the Savoy? Maybe I went to the Savoy. No, no, no. Dickie Wells got me the job down at Smalls with Elmder Snowden in '31. Then they let Snowden go, and Charlie Johnson came in, and they kept me. I was the only one he kept, you know. And I stayed there with him, and then I ended up going to the Savoy. And I was in the Savoy because they started... Oh, we made an…

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: We had a lot of Ellington's men on them.

ctx.x: Whoever was in town we would use.
We had a lot of Ellington's men on them.
Yep. I got some with Helen Humes; I got some with Charlie Christian; whoever was in town, you used them on bass, and was gracious that remembered me from Chicago and used me.
